name: Tuck Front Lever
summary: An isometric calisthenics hold where the torso is suspended horizontally beneath a bar with the knees tucked tightly to the chest.

setup: Grasp a pull-up bar with an overhand (pronated) grip, hands spaced shoulder-width apart.
Hang with your arms fully extended and engage your shoulders by depressing the scapulae downward.
steps: Pull your knees tightly into your chest into a compact tucked position.
Pull down through straight arms using your lats to rotate your body backward until your back is parallel to the floor.
Maintain straight elbows, depressed shoulders, and a flat horizontal back.
Hold the horizontal position for the target duration, then lower under control back to a hang.
instructions.breathing: Maintain continuous, shallow diaphragmatic breathing while bracing your core throughout the hold.
cues: Push the bar down toward your hips
Keep the knees glued to the chest
Level your back with the floor

common_faults.fault: Bending the elbows to compensate for lat weakness.
common_faults.correction: Keep the elbows completely locked; regress to banded tuck holds or active hangs if arm extension cannot be maintained.
Pull down harder through the shoulders and tuck the knees tighter to raise the pelvis in line with the shoulders.

common_faults.fault: Excessive thoracic rounding and internally collapsed shoulders.
common_faults.correction: Depress and slightly retract your shoulder blades to keep the chest proud and upper back stable.

precautions: Ensure the pull-up bar or suspension anchor is securely fastened before inverting.
Exit the hold immediately if elbow tendon pain or sudden shoulder strain occurs.
